This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 22.01.2020 passed by MACT (WN), Mandleshwar in MACC No.146/2018 seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in dispute.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Ajim Pathan, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,24,800/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.2,00,000/- (i.e. Rs.5000 p.mx12 - 1/3 (personal expenses) x 5(multiplier) ) Consortium -Rs.40,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 Medical expenses -Rs.54,800/-

TOTAL Rs.3,24,800/-
 -------------------

2 3.

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding just and proper amount of compensation as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side, hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper amount of compensation in the case.
The Tribunal has committed an error in awarding only Rs.40,000/- under the head of consortium to five of the dependents.

The Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram & others has interpreted the term "consortium" to be a compendious term which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium as well as filial consortium.

sentences.text:
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort,
guidance, solace and affection of the deceased which is a loss to his whole family.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Loss of dependency -Rs.2,00,000/- (i.e. Rs.5000 p.mx12 - 1/3 (personal expenses) x 5(multiplier) ) Medical expenses -Rs.54,800/-
 Consortium -Rs.2,20,000/- (i.e. Rs.4400  Loss of estate -Rs.16,500/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.16,500/-
 ----------------
 TOTAL Rs.5,07,800/-
 ===========
6.
Hence, the just and proper amount of compensation in the case is Rs.5,07,800/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.3,24,800/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,83,000/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.1,83,000/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

The appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.1,50,000/- and paid the Court fees accordingly, however,
for the remaining amount of Rs.33,000/- the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.
